title: Believers have a ready remedy for future falls—not already-remitted futures; Maresius’s dangerous speech
source_text: XXIV. Verum est quidem illos qui fide Christum amplexi sunt, in Christo paratum remedium habere ad peccata etiam futura: hoc est illos certos esse posse, quod quum in peccata quaelibet inciderint, eorum veniam & condonationem sint per Christi mortem adepturi, modo per renovatos poenitentiae & fidei actus ad eam confugiant, ut panaceam illam ad novum istud malum quo prementur applicent. Sed inde non sequitur peccata futura jam illis remissa esse, sed solum per Christi gratiam remittenda, modo illi sibi non desint. Neque aliud sibi velle videntur illi ipsi qui aliter ac nos hac parte loquuntur: cum dicant per varios fidei actus subinde elicitos, nostram absolutionem & justificationem applicari & extendi ad quotidiana nostra peccata, reflectendo versus meritum Christi, & reconciliationem nobis in eo partam & oblatam. Ut videre est apud Samuelem Maresium loco 11. Th. 58. Si enim nostra justificatio per novos fidei actus applicatur atque extenditur ad peccata in quae quotidie labimur, ante actus illos novos ad ea se non actu extendebat, nec erat iis actu applicata: ac proinde peccata illa antequam committerentur, ex mente doctorum illorum virorum, actu remissa nondum erant. Sed fatendum est illos periculose loqui, & praetextum ac occasionem praebere doctrinam nostram calumniandi: ut manifestum est ex iis quae inde contra Reformatos deducere conatur author ille famosus, qui Christianae Ethices subversae illos, magna cum verborum pompa, non ita pridem accusavit.
pass_a_gloss: It is indeed true that those who have embraced Christ by faith have in Christ a ready remedy even for future sins: that is, that they can be certain that when they have fallen into any sins whatever, they will obtain their pardon and forgiveness through Christ’s death, provided that through renewed acts of repentance and faith they flee to it, so as to apply that panacea to this new evil by which they are pressed. But from that it does not follow that future sins are already remitted to them, but only that they are to be remitted through Christ’s grace, provided they do not fail themselves. Nor do those themselves who speak otherwise than we do on this point seem to mean anything else: since they say that through various acts of faith repeatedly elicited our absolution and justification are applied and extended to our daily sins, by reflecting toward Christ’s merit and the reconciliation obtained and offered to us in him—as may be seen in Samuel Maresius, locus 11, thesis 58. For if our justification through new acts of faith is applied and extended to the sins into which we daily fall, before those new acts it did not actually extend itself to them, nor was it actually applied to them; and therefore those sins, before they were committed, were not yet actually remitted even on the mind of those learned men. But it must be confessed that they speak dangerously and furnish a pretext and occasion for calumniating our doctrine—as is manifest from what that famous author who not long ago, with great pomp of words, accused them of the subversion of Christian ethics tries to draw from it against the Reformed.
pass_b_english: Ready Christ-remedy for future falls requires renewed faith-repentance acts—not already-done pardon.
Even Maresius’s ‘extend justification by new faith-acts’ implies pre-act non-application; absolute speech invites calumny.

choices.why: Future sins: promissory, not already actual.
